reason: The browser mirror of the settings description, the per-entry write queue and the settings slot types are not built. A settings card is an effect of a host component registered with settingspage.Registry, or is generated from the entry's Go config type, and it reads and writes through area A07's settings.Forms with the revision check kept.

The Settings panel becomes the server-rendered page /settings with one address per section, and the General section becomes a region that features contribute rows to. The connection indicator and release prompt belong to area C1, version and first run to area A25, and the update-channel row and the native open-file action are dropped with the desktop application.

The Models page becomes a settings section rendered from the model runtime's route list, with a written card per route, a generated fold for every other live field and a separate write-only key form over the credential routes. The first-run credential step and the welcome notice move to area A25's setup page.

The account section, sign-in, sign-out confirmation, profile and balance become a host-rendered panel over area A17's account and authorization services, with sign-in started by a link the person clicks. The desktop introduction, the embedded vendor page and the prefilled third-party questionnaire are not built.

Notice cards become a host-rendered contribution to the shell's notice region, fed by area A17's poll, which is a setting that is off by default and obeys the off-switch. The browser polls nothing and reports nothing; the host reports an interaction only while the setting is on.

A browser package that exists to give one number a page, with an empty host half so the client loader has a row to serve. In Go the parallel cap is a live field of a config struct and gets a generated card with no UI code.

A companion package for two shell fields. The composed shell entry's own Go config type (bash or PowerShell) is described by settings.Forms and rendered as a generated card, so no package or template is needed.

Depth and capacity are live fields on a generated card. The route selection is one written field whose options come from the model runtime's route list on each render, saved through the same revision-checked form.

The provider menus and provider settings become part of the connections section: menus list area A15's providers with each availability reason and show what automatic selection resolves to, and each provider's settings are a card on its own config entry.

The upload switch is no longer a row among General preferences. It is one row of the sharing page, which lists every sender registered with area A18's gate, and it writes area A05's logupload setting.

The Plugins page becomes server-rendered pages over area A21's plugins.Manager, area A22's plugin descriptors and area A18's inventory. Installing by running pnpm, registry probing, install progress, versions and updates are not built; adding a plugin is inspecting a local directory, consenting to its report and granting capabilities.

The Discover tab browses index sources and installs or updates bundles from them. DH-ADR-13 decides that plugins come from local directories with no download, discovery or auto-update, so there is no index to browse; area A21 records the rules a later registry must keep.

The host registry, its remote and the browser half are not built. Area A15's account view is already the host-computed display, and the connections section renders its phase and actions as given; an authorization page is a link in the answer to the Connect form.

The composer control and the picker become a host fragment and one form over area A17's preset service, which also states how many session grants a switch revokes. The default for new sessions is an ordinary field of the permission presets card in the General section.

The skill tool row becomes a card registered with area C4's card registry and drawn from the logged call and result only. The preview becomes a fragment over area A14's skill registry through the sanitising renderer, and a skills list with sources and diagnostics is added. Skill candidates in the slash menu are a completion source of area C3; the browser cache is not built.

Vendor notices are still plain text with two actions (dismiss, open the account section), and a failed poll still keeps the current cards. The Go page escapes the vendor's text and offers the same closed set of actions.
justification: The vendor's notice format carries plain text and these actions only; rendering richer content would mean trusting vendor markup inside an owner's page. Polling is now off by default, so the limit is met only by a user who opted in.

reason: The page has no phase vocabulary of its own. It renders area A15's account view, whose closed status set separates states upstream folds into five phases, for example needs re-authorisation from never connected and waiting for credentials from failed.
Account views are derived from configuration and saved grants, not from a live registrant, so an entry that failed to load still shows its account with the failure and a sign-out action.
Opening a page reads host state and starts nothing. A check or probe is an explicit button that calls the fleet once; a test counts the fleet's calls while the section is opened.
There is no account registry to load. The account list is a method of the MCP fleet, and the section shows accounts only when that list is not empty.

No script opens a tab after an answer arrives. Starting an authorization answers a fragment that holds an ordinary link to the authorization address; a click on a link is a user gesture, which no pop-up blocker stops, and the link stays in the page while the attempt is pending.
The default preset is a live field of the permission presets config, not a browser contribution, so the settings page, a layer file and any other configuration surface edit the same value.
Automatic review still cannot be chosen as the default for new sessions, and it is offered in the picker only when the experimental review layer registers it, behind a confirmation.
justification: Area A17 reserves the name for the experimental review layer and its config validation requires a default to name a shipped preset; a default that depends on an experimental component would make new sessions fail when it is absent.

reason: Labels and descriptions of the shipped presets are message-catalogue keys resolved in the request's language, so they cannot disagree. Text an operator wrote for a preset of their own is data and is shown verbatim, by the rule that data is never translated.
The limit is about a ping race between two npm registries, which exists only because plugins are npm packages that pnpm downloads. The Go harness downloads no plugin and contacts no registry.

There is no installation run and no host log file to point at. Adding a plugin is one inspection and one layer write, and a refusal renders the inspection's problem list in the page, also for a browser on another machine.

No request is tracked in the page. An operation is a short synchronous call whose result is host state: after a reload the list shows whether the entry exists and its status, and the inventory keeps a history of recent phase changes.
The bundle concept is gone. The page lists every composed entry from the inventory and every plugin process from the plugin host, so nothing that runs is left off the page.
A row shows the status with its reason: the failing stage and message of a plugin, or the entry's current diagnostic from the inventory, not only a phase.
The limit is that one pnpm command runs at a time. No package manager runs in the Go harness; an add is one write of the profile layer, serialised by the layer lock for a few milliseconds.

A version picker would list npm registry versions for a pnpm spec. A Go plugin is a local directory with one manifest version, shown on its page; replacing the directory and approving it again is the only way to change versions.
The limit is where the chosen npm registry is remembered. There is no registry choice because nothing is downloaded.
The limit is that reading the registry configuration runs pnpm and fails on a machine without it. No view or operation of the Go plugins page runs a package manager.

The limit is about which installed copies the Discover tab can update. There is no market and no update operation; the page shows a banner when a directory changed after approval, and approving the new content is the update.

No market detail document is fetched or rendered. A plugin's page shows its manifest and inspection report as escaped text; if a plugin's own README is ever shown it passes area C4's sanitising renderer, which omits raw HTML by rule.

The page requests no remote icon. The content security policy allows images from the host's own origin only, and a plugin is shown with a glyph and its name, so no image host learns the user's address.

Profile and balance still come from the vendor's web endpoints through the host, are read when the panel opens, fail independently and never show a manufactured zero; usage and top-up remain links that carry no token.
justification: The vendor offers no other interface for these facts, and area A17's account service uses the same endpoints. The page limits the cost: nothing is fetched until the person opens the panel, and each card states its own failure.

reason: The limit describes the completion marker of the desktop introduction. That introduction is not built, and first run in Go stores no completion: area A25's setup page computes whether a model is usable each time.
The illustration sets belong to the desktop introduction, which is dropped with the desktop application, so there is no artwork to keep in step with language and theme.

Vendor sign-in still needs a loopback address, because the vendor accepts only loopback callback origins. What changes is the failure: when the host's public address is not loopback the panel explains this and offers no start control, instead of a generic retry state.
justification: The accepted callback origins are set by the vendor's authorization service and cannot be changed from this side; a deployment behind another address adds an API key instead.

reason: The limit is a conflict between an embedded vendor page and the desktop caption menu. Neither exists: vendor pages open as ordinary links in a new tab.

The card is generated from the config type, so every field its owner marks live appears without a UI change. The composed agents list is not live and is shown as file-only with the layer file's path, instead of being absent.

Behaviour under a phone's software keyboard is still not validated on real devices. The risk is lower because settings is an ordinary scrolling page, not a fixed-height panel, so the browser's own scrolling brings a focused field into view.
justification: The project has no device lab; the real-browser scenarios run desktop browsers with a narrow viewport, which does not reproduce native keyboard panning.

reason: A row is still contributed by the component that owns the preference, by design, but a preference no longer disappears when no row was written for it: every live field has a generated card, shown under Advanced when nobody placed it.
The limit is about a badge in the desktop window's caption on Windows. There is no desktop window, caption or desktop update badge; the update notice is a region of area A25's product status.

The written card covers the common fields and a generated fold below it lists every other live field of the route's config type, so timeouts and advanced fields are editable without a hand-written editor.

Removal still deletes a key only when the row can show nobody else uses it, but a retained key is no longer invisible: the credentials list shows every reference with its source and the entries that name it, so an unused stored key can be seen and deleted there.
The custom-endpoint form writes a keyed route on any of the four protocols area A04 drives, the Anthropic Messages protocol among them, so an endpoint of any vendor can be declared from the page.
The provider picker is now a host-filtered search with the custom endpoint pinned, which removes the mode switch, but it lists product names only where the embedded catalogue has them.
justification: A display name per vendor is a field of area A04's embedded catalogue, which its specification does not define yet; this area requests it and shows the route identifier meanwhile.

reason: Discovery is a method of the adapter seam, and all four protocols of the first plan can list models, so the page asks whichever adapter serves the route and needs no per-protocol code. A later sign-in component answers through the same method.
The list is the runtime's route list, so every registered route has a row. A route that no config entry of the page can edit is shown read-only and names the component that provides it.

The row is generated from the senders registered with area A18's gate. A profile that does not compose the upload component has no such sender, cannot send, and correctly has no row; nothing is shown as present but unavailable.

The card is generated from the composed entry's own config type, so a PowerShell host shows the fields of the PowerShell type, including the ones bash does not have, instead of the same two fields on both.
The page keeps no copy of the route catalogue. The options are read from the model runtime when the card is rendered, and the region is replaced when the runtime announces a change of models.

The menu shows what automatic selection resolves to now, from area A15's availability check for the route, including a provider chosen by an environment expression and the ambiguous case, which is shown as a warning before a tool call fails.

Each provider's availability carries a reason code, such as a missing credential or no signed-in account, and the page shows it beside the billing choice; the host can read the account and key state that the upstream page could not.

Configuration is shared by every admitted browser on purpose. A choice that should differ per browser now has a home of its own: shortcut overrides stay on the device, a layout preference may be declared per platform class, and area A25 has a fragment for what is specific to one browser.
A card is found by the tool name in the logged call, and history pages are aligned to turns, so a result is always drawn with its call. The skill card is registered globally and needs no live agent.
A skill reference in a message is still plain text: a hand-typed name is the same reference as a picked one, and the host judges the sent text.
justification: A model request must be rebuilt from the log as it was sent, and area A14 resolves an invocation on the host from that text; a chip is presentation owned by area C3's composer and must not become a second truth.

reason: There is no prewarmed browser cache to race. The menu is a host fragment computed from the skill registry for each request, so the first keystroke already lists the skills.

Nothing is cached in the page. Area A14's filesystem provider watches the skill directories and announces a change, and the skills region of an open session is replaced then; the next menu request reads the registry anyway.
Highlighting no longer depends on a browser-side lexicon that can be emptied. Area C3's host computes the spans of a draft from the current registry whenever the draft is saved or rendered.

The credentialOnboarding switch decided whether the browser offered a first-run key step. First run is area A25's host-rendered setup page, whose setup.Config.Enabled turns it off for a deployment provisioned by configuration; the models section has no such field.

The poll interval configured a browser poller. Polling is done by area A17's account component under its Notifications setting, off by default; the interval is requested of that area's config and this area declares no struct.

The schema holds the progress of the desktop introduction and the address of a third-party questionnaire. The introduction is dropped with the desktop application, and a questionnaire prefilled with account and device data is data leaving the machine with no preview.
The three fields tune the probe that races two npm registries. No registry is contacted because plugins are local directories.

No service key replaces ctx.connectorAccounts in this area. Its registration contract is area A15's connector package (AccountView, AccountSource) and its listing is mcp.Service.Accounts(); the connections section renders those values and calls the fleet's own operations.
The service races the response time of two public npm registries to recommend one for an installation. The Go harness installs nothing from a registry, so there is nothing to recommend.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep its rule, drop its mechanism. The rule (the host decides phase, text, buttons and confirmations; the browser only displays and opens the authorization page) is what every server-rendered page does. The registry, its remote and the shared browser half exist because client plugins cannot share code; area A15's account view is the host-computed display, and the page renders it. The one browser duty left, opening the authorization page, becomes a link the person clicks.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep. Authentication is the identity boundary and locality selects nothing, so every admitted browser and every process on the home reads and writes one settings document, arbitrated by a revision. The note's one locality-dependent control, opening the configuration file in a native editor, is not built; the page shows the file's path.

title: A settings card is an effect of a host component, generated from its config type unless a template is registered; settings is one page with an address per section
One form protocol: staged, revision-checked, validated only on the host, and a conflict never loses the draft
A save says what the loader did; a restart is previewed and confirmed; everything else is honestly file-only
Everything that leaves the machine is switched on one page that is generated from the gate
The plugins page manages local directories: inspect, consent on the report, grant; there is no market
Model routes are listed from the runtime; a key is its own write-only form and is never rendered back
The host decides what an account shows; an authorization page is a link the person clicks; vendor traffic needs an action or an opt-in
Choosing a preset is one host form over the preset service; grants are shown, not reimplemented
Skills are rendered from the host registry on request; a skill call is drawn from the log alone
Any component's live settings can be edited in the browser, and a bad or stale edit changes nothing
The General section holds the everyday preferences, whoever owns them
One page shows every kind of data that can leave the machine, each with its switch, and one switch that stops them all
A person adds a model provider, stores its key and edits its models, and no page ever shows the key
A person signs in to the vendor account, sees profile and balance, signs out, and may opt in to notices
A person adds a plugin from a local directory after reading what it asks for, and manages it afterwards
A person sees MCP servers, links connector accounts and chooses web providers, with the reason when something is unusable
A person chooses how much the agent may do, for this session and for new ones, and sees the grants in force
A person sees which skills a session has, where each comes from and why one is hidden, and reads a skill before using it
A setting that needs a restart can be changed in the browser after a preview of what restarts
A malformed section or card fails registration, and a card leaves with its owner
Every entry with live fields renders a generated card with text in both languages
A posted card decodes to set, reset and clear operations for changed fields only
An invalid, stale, shadowed or unsavable edit writes nothing and keeps the draft
The save outcome reports what the loader did, including a restart and a later failure
A change made in another tab or process replaces an open card, and a non-owner is refused
General rows are contributed in order, and language and default preset are stored
The sharing page has exactly one row per registered sender, in the sender's words
The off-switch, the environment lock and the all-off defaults of a fresh home
Every model route has a row, and the catalogue picker searches
No response of this area contains a stored or rejected secret
A route is created with its credential reference in one write and removed without orphaning or over-deleting a key
Route check and model discovery run once per request and show classified results
The account panel: sign-in link, pending attempt, independent failures, no token in links
Account notices cause no request while off and are escaped plain text while on
Plugin and entry rows show status with its reason, grants and a changed-source banner
Adding a plugin passes exactly the ticked capabilities for the shown digest, and no market route exists
Each plugin management action is one idempotent manager operation, owner only
Account views and provider menus are rendered as the host gives them, and opening the section probes nothing
The preset picker lists presets, states the grants a switch revokes and refuses a non-owner
The skills list, a safe preview, live replacement, and a tool card that depends on the log only
A restart edit is previewed without writing and applied only at the previewed revision
A live setting is edited from two browsers and a second process, and a bad edit changes nothing
The sharing page turns each kind on and off against a recording collector, and the off-switch stops all of them
A provider is added with a real key that never appears in a page, a response or a log
A plugin directory is inspected, granted in part, run, changed, approved again and removed
Accounts are linked through the system browser from the account panel and the connections section
A preset switch revokes a session grant, and a skill is listed, changed on disk and called
